# Development revision

The first screen found small incremental value for exact field containment. Errors inspected only in the original training-file calibration subset included records sharing long topic fragments, accented or encoded names, and similarly titled records with contradictory labels. There were 13 false positives and 1 false negative in ACM, and 83 and 39 respectively in Google Scholar. Examples motivated an ordered title-prefix feature because the corruption can append another field after an intact title. The new question is whether order and cross-field alignment add signal after accounting for whole-string similarity.

Use the existing train/calibration partition, existing classifier, fixed threshold-fitting rule, and both already-used development files. Run the published SecondString SoftTFIDF implementation using its default Jaro–Winkler threshold. Compare the earlier full candidate, that candidate plus character edit similarities, and the same expanded model with unordered flattened soft-token matching. Evaluate two further ablations with either ordered title prefix recovery or field-resolved one-to-one token assignment added to the flattened control. Combine both for the proposed method. Keep the original one absolute F1 percentage point advance criterion against every method on both releases. No test files are acquired. These development comparisons alone cannot establish superiority for a paper.
